हिंदुओं की समस्या यह है कि उन्होंने अपने ग्रंथ नहीं पढे हैं, और वह 2014 के बाद ही हिंदू बने हैं। ना उन्होंने वेद दर्शन उपनिषद रामायण महाभारत पढे हैं। यहां तक की उन्होंने गीता भी नहीं पढी है।
लोग सोचते हैं कि रामायण पूरी तरह वाल्मीकि रामायण पर बनाई जानी चाहिए थी, पर सच कहूं तो हिंदू उसे झेल भी नहीं पाएगा, और डायरेक्टर प्रोड्यूसर को मारने से पहले खुद अपने नाखूनों से अपना सीना फाड़ लेगा।
कुछ लोग अभी बकवास कर रहे हैं कि माता सीता श्री राम को सीधे राम क्यों बोल रही हैं? मैंने कहा न यह लोग 2014 के बाद हिंदू बने हैं। और तब से केवल हिंदू नाम के कारण माइलेज ले रहे हैं। अच्छा वक्त बीता पिछले एक दशक में, बढ़िया होता एक दो धार्मिक पुस्तक पढ़ लेते तो आज उछल-उछल कर हिंदुत्व की बात न करनी पड़ती। पढ़ते रहे हैं रामचरितमानस और सब कुछ चाहिए वाल्मीकि रामायण के हिसाब से!

माता सीता एक दो बार नहीं बल्कि कई बार उनको राम और राघव कह कर बुलाती हैं। अब तुमको यह वोकिज्म लग रहा है। क्योंकि अब तुम हर चीज को अपने ग्रंथ के नहीं बल्कि ट्रोल्स और पश्चिम की नजर से देखने लगे हो। अब हम एक प्राइम हिन्दुत्व में जी रहे हैं जहाँ हम अपने धर्म ग्रंथ की भाषा आदि अपने-अपने पैमाने पर सेट करके ही मानेंगे। उसी से पता लगेगा कि सबसे बड़ा हिंदू कौन है।

कुछ लोग रामानंद सागर को ही वाल्मीकि समझकर कह रहे हैं कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने माता सीता को कभी हाथ में अस्त्र-शस्त्र लेते हुए नहीं दिखाया इसलिए अब जो भी दिखाएगा वह हिंदुत्व विरोधी हो जाएगा। जबकि वह यह भूल जाते हैं की माता सीता एक क्षत्राणी थी और वह धनुर्विद्या तथा तलवार चलाने में महारथी थी। अगर वह भगवान शिव का पिनाक उठाकर रख सकती थी तो क्या वह तलवार नहीं चला सकती थी? लेकिन यहां भी लोगों को हॉलीवुड की नकल पहले दिखने लग जाती है अपने ग्रंथ नहीं।

फिर कुछ लोगों ने आपत्ति जताई कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने तो विवाह स्थल पर ही परशुराम संवाद दिखाया था इसलिए जो यह नहीं दिखाएगा वह भी हिंदू विरोधी होगा जबकि वाल्मीकि रामायण में यह प्रकरण मिथिला में ही परंतु बारात वापसी के मार्ग में बताया गया है।

फिर कुछ लोगों को समस्या हुई की इसमें तो सूर्पनखा का नाक काटते समय फेमिनिज्म को बढ़ावा दिया गया है जबकि रामानंद सागर की रामायण में स्वयं राम लक्ष्मण से कहते हैं कि तुमने अच्छा नहीं किया।

फिर यह बात उठा दी गई कि रावण का महिमा मंडन किया जा रहा है, उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया गया। जबकि रामानंद सागर ने स्वयं हनुमान जी से और श्री राम जी से रावण का महिमा मंडन करवाया था। किसी ने उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया हालाँकि वो था। हर चीज दिखाई नहीं जाती, पढी सब जाती हैं। परंतु रामानंद सागर की रामायण देखते समय हमारी आंखों में आंसू आ जाते हैं और हम कहते हैं कि यह हमारा इतिहास है इस पर हमें गर्व है इसने वर्ल्ड रिकॉर्ड बना दिया।

यह किसी फिल्म का प्रमोशन नहीं बल्कि मैं इस पोस्ट के जरिए वाल्मीकि रामायण का प्रमोशन करना चाहता हूं। जितने में आप एक टिकट लेंगे उससे कम पैसे में एक वाल्मीकि रामायण आ जाएगी जो आपके घर में अगले 50 साल तक रहेगी और आपकी पीढ़ियां उसको पढेंगी। लेकिन समस्या यही है कि पढ़ना आसान नहीं होता और हिंदू के लिए तो बिल्कुल भी नहीं, पर फिर भी मैं कहूंगा...
अच्छा होगा कभी वाल्मीकि रामायण पढ़ो। 🙏

Advait Energy Transitions: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Advait provides power transmission products and is expanding into battery storage and green hydrogen. Profit grew 89% and its order book is up 47%.

Q2 FY27 (consolidated)
Revenue: ₹221 Cr (+40.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹32 Cr (+84.4% YoY), margin 14.5% (vs 11%)
PAT: ₹19 Cr (+88.5% YoY), margin 8.7%
H1 FY27 revenue: ₹400 Cr (+45.4% YoY)
H1 FY27 PAT: ₹34 Cr (+77.9% YoY)
Order book (including L1): about ₹1,575 Cr (+47% YoY)

1.  Order book growing fast-
The order book, including projects where Advait is the lowest bidder, grew 47% to about ₹1,575 Cr. It completed orders worth about ₹400 Cr in H1. This gives healthy revenue visibility.

2.  Transmission business steady-
Advait won distribution orders from Gujarat power utilities, including about ₹52 Cr from DGVCL. It also won orders for emergency restoration systems, OPGW (power lines with built-in optical fibre) and stringing tools. India's continued investment in transmission supports demand.

3.  Battery storage push-
Advait won a 150 MW / 300 MWh standalone battery storage project in Junagadh. A 2.5 GWh battery manufacturing plant, expandable to 5 GWh, should start by Q4 FY27. Machinery orders have already been placed.

4.  Green hydrogen progress-
Advait's electrolyser technology, which splits water into hydrogen, is being tested in a 5 MW program. It is engaging with over 13 Indian green hydrogen players. It has also signed an offtake agreement with battery maker Hithium for its upcoming orders.

5.  New integrated factory-
Phase 1 of the integrated manufacturing facility at Gangad, Gujarat should start by Q4 FY27. It will support transmission, substation and renewable energy products.

6.  Big long-term ambition-
Management has outlined a target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years, about 7 times FY26 revenue. It says this depends on investor and funding support. Margins should improve as more revenue comes from manufactured products.

Key Guidance
FY27 capex of ₹300-350 Cr
Battery plant and Gangad facility operational by Q4 FY27
Long-term target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years

Wockhardt revenue up 24% to ₹969 Cr, but profit falls 11% on margin squeeze

👉 Wockhardt reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹969 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 23.9% from ₹782 Cr a year earlier and 4.3% higher than ₹929 Cr in Q1. Total income was ₹980 Cr. Net profit, however, fell 11% year on year to ₹73 Cr, and dropped 31.8% from ₹107 Cr in the previous quarter.

👉 Operating margin fell to 7.4% from 12.1% in Q1 and 11.3% a year earlier, as total expenses rose 27% YoY to ₹907 Cr from ₹712 Cr. Cost of materials consumed climbed to ₹243 Cr from ₹159 Cr. Profit excluding other income was ₹62 Cr, down from ₹70 Cr a year ago.

👉 Other income fell to ₹11 Cr from ₹31 Cr in Q1, and profit before tax was ₹73 Cr, against ₹116 Cr in Q1 and ₹91 Cr a year ago. No exceptional items were booked this quarter, unlike the six months last year, which carried a ₹97 Cr charge. Six-month revenue rose 24.9% to ₹1,898 Cr, with six-month net profit at ₹180 Cr against a loss of ₹26 Cr.

👉 The company record shows FY26 revenue of ₹3,373 Cr beat management's ₹3,033 Cr guidance, though net debt to equity came in at 0.10% against a guided 0.01%. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating to A- (Stable) in May, citing improved financial performance. Q2 is the second quarterly result since then, and operating margin is now the weakest of the three quarters shown here.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans to launch Zaynich in the US, India and Europe and double human insulin capacity, according to its June earnings call.

👉 Road blocker: Operating margin fell to 7.4% from 12.1% in Q1, while cost of materials consumed rose 53% YoY to ₹243 Cr.

#Carborundum Universal vs #Wendt India

A note to help investors work through the symphony-cacophony of Murugappa Group’s success stories.

Carborundum Universal (#CUMI) is the stronger choice for most investors seeking exposure to the abrasives and industrial materials theme. Wendt India works better as a smaller satellite holding.

CUMI is a diversified materials company under the Murugappa Group. It operates across abrasives, electrominerals, and ceramics or refractories. Trailing 12-month sales stand near Rs 5,400 cr with a market capitalisation of about Rs 19,000 cr. Trailing PAT is around Rs 188 cr. The stock trades at roughly 75 to 100 times trailing earnings. Return on equity is about 7% and return on capital employed near 10 to 11%. Debt is low.

In the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 17% year on year and profit after tax rose 23%.

Wendt India is a focused player in super abrasives and precision grinding tools. Trailing 12-month sales are about Rs 270 cr with a market cap near Rs 1,380 cr. Trailing PAT is roughly Rs 20 cr. The stock trades near 70x trailing earnings.

Return on equity is about 5%. The company is nearly debt free. In the September 2026 quarter, revenue grew 28% year on year to about Rs 72.5 cr and profit after tax more than doubled to Rs 5.5 cr.

💯 CUMI owns a 37.5% stake in 🤝 Wendt.

✨ CUMI offers better diversification across products and geographies, higher liquidity, and stronger absolute earnings power. It also gives indirect exposure to Wendt’s super abrasives business.

Wendt has shown cleaner recent operating recovery in its core segment, but its smaller size and lower liquidity increase volatility.

Both stocks look expensive on current trailing earnings because profits have been under pressure. Further upside depends on sustained recovery in margins and volumes.

Sector tailwinds from manufacturing growth, defence, semiconductors, and shifts in Chinese competition support the theme over the medium term.

My way:

Prefer CUMI as the core holding. Consider Wendt only in a limited size if you want concentrated exposure to precision tooling and can accept higher volatility.

Accumulate on dips rather than at current levels. Monitor the next set of quarterly results for confirmation of margin improvement.

Sona BLW Precision Forgings

An impressive quarter, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Revenue: 1,547 Cr (+35% YoY)
EBITDA: 356 Cr (+23% YoY)
PAT: 223 Cr (+29% YoY)
BEV revenue: +129% YoY, now contributing 51% of automotive revenue.
Order book: 25,100 Cr, with 3,600 Cr of fresh orders.

What makes this quarter interesting is the changing business mix.
EV traction motors are scaling up, differential assemblies are recovering, and newer businesses such as railway systems, sensors and robotics are opening additional growth opportunities.
EV and Robotics/Physical AI already account for 65% of the order book. Importantly, 31 of the company's 75 EPIC programs are yet to enter production.

Is this an inflection?
There are early signs of a meaningful revenue and product-mix inflection, with new programs transitioning towards commercialisation and stronger cash generation.
However, an earnings-margin inflection is not yet evident. EBITDA margin contracted from 25.3% to 23%, reflecting product mix and input-cost pressures.

The next trigger is whether strong revenue growth translates into operating leverage and margin expansion.

Sona Comstar increasingly looks like a broader mobility technology platform rather than just a traditional automotive component manufacturer.

EOD wrap, 2 Nov 2026

A 1.68% Nifty day, the best in a month, and almost all of it was one stock.

Granules India drew a USFDA Form 483 with eleven observations at its Gagillapur plant. The detail that matters is that this was the first inspection of that site since the warning letter dated February 2025, so it was a test of whether remediation took, and eleven observations is not a pass. There are real mitigants. None of the observations touch data integrity or cross contamination, they cover investigations, change control, qualification and documentation, and the company says there is no impact on manufacture or distribution. The same board meeting cleared a decent quarter, revenue up 20.3% and profit up 39.2%. The stock opened flat, ran up a percent, then sold off to close down 2.27%. A 39% profit rise bought about an hour. What matters next is the classification, not the next print.

Index wrap. Nifty 50 closed 23,440.80, up 1.68%, a one month high and a third straight gain. Sensex 75,692.78, up 1.66%. Bank Nifty lagged badly at up only 0.58%. Oil and Gas rose 5.95% and Metal 3.21%, while Media, IT, Private Bank and Pharma finished lower.

Reliance alone contributed roughly 198 of the Nifty's 388 points, up 11.6% on its record refining quarter, its sharpest single day gain since April 2020. Brent fell about 4% to around 108.5 dollars on a third day of talks in Doha.

Breadth was positive and hollow at the same time. 2,445 advances against 1,164 declines, yet 143 new 52 week lows against just 57 new highs. Nearly three new lows for every new high on a two to one advance day is a rally off a weak base, not a re-rating. On flows, the 2 November provisionals are not out yet. Friday is the last confirmed session, foreign investors buying 3,599 crore against domestic institutions selling 818 crore.

The other move worth attention. Sterlite Technologies, HFCL and MTAR all locked at 5% lower circuit, a second day running, now 22 to 25% off their October highs, on no news at all. Year to date they are up 664%, 151% and 171% against a Sensex down 11.6%. Three names hitting circuit together on a strong index day tends to matter more a week later than it does today.

Tomorrow brings the US midterms, called the near term swing factor by both the oil and currency desks, and crude is now the cleanest single input into the December RBI meeting.

Market commentary, not investment advice.

Market Alignment: The company is closely tracking India's national mission goals, which provide incentives for production and infrastructure. ⚡ Advait Energy Transitions | Nov 2026 Concall
🏭 Management’s big transition: from EPC execution toward a manufacturing-led platform!

📊 Q2 revenue: ₹221cr | 🟢⬆️ 40.8% YoY
💰 EBITDA: ₹32cr | 🟢⬆️ 84.4%
💵 PAT: ₹19cr | 🟢⬆️ 88.5%

1️⃣ 🎯 FY27 outlook reiterated
Management remains aligned with its ~₹1,100cr revenue target. Against H1 revenue of ~₹400cr, this implies approximately ₹700cr of execution in H2.

🚀 The longer-term ambition remains ₹5,000cr revenue over five years.

2️⃣ 📚 Order visibility—with an important qualifier
Order book including L1 positions stood at ~₹1,750cr at September-end, 🟢⬆️ 47% YoY.

✅ Management highlighted ~₹400cr of orders executed in H1.
👀 L1 positions still require conversion into firm awards.

3️⃣ 🔄 Manufacturing mix transformation
Manufacturing currently contributes ~38%; management targets 70–75% from FY29.

The company also aims for a more balanced Power Transmission Solutions (PTS) and New & Renewable Energy (NRE) mix, moving toward ~50:50 over 2–3 years.

🏗️ At full capacity, management believes PTS manufacturing could support sales exceeding ₹2,500cr—a capacity-based estimate.

4️⃣ 🛠️ Capex and integrated facility
H1 capex: ~₹101cr.
Further H2 capex planned: ~₹140cr.

🎯 Phase 1 of the integrated Gujarat manufacturing facility is targeted for Q4 FY27, supporting transmission, substation solutions and renewable-energy infrastructure.

5️⃣ 🔋 BESS manufacturing takes shape
A 2.5 GWh facility, expandable to 5 GWh, is targeted to become operational by Q4 FY27. Final plant and machinery orders have been placed.

📊 First-year utilisation expectation: 40–60%.
💰 At full utilisation, management cited revenue potential of ~₹1,000–1,100cr per GWh, depending on scope.

✅ The 150 MW/300 MWh Junagadh BESS project adds an execution opportunity alongside the manufacturing build-out.

6️⃣ 🧪 Hydrogen: phased scaling
The existing 30 MW electrolyzer assembly platform is intended to scale to 150 MW, with infrastructure expandable toward 1 GW by FY29.

Management cited ₹600–1,000cr revenue potential at 150 MW, depending on scope, utilisation and orders.

✅ A 300 kW project has been completed.
✅ Supply for a 1 MW project is complete; commissioning is expected this quarter.

👀 The precise commissioning quarter for the 150 MW expansion needs clarification.

7️⃣ 📈 Margin ambition
Management expects broadly similar near-term profitability, while aspiring to ~15% group EBITDA margin once manufacturing facilities are established and ramped up.

Procurement bookings have helped manage inflation, but commissioning and utilisation remain central to the margin plan.

8️⃣ 🏦 Funding the expansion
Gross borrowings were stated at ~₹280cr, with D/E at 0.86x.

Management is considering an equity raise in Q3/Q4 FY27 for working capital and indicated a D/E target of 0.5–0.7x, acknowledging fluctuations during asset creation.

👀 Watch fundraising terms, dilution, collections and returns on new assets.

9️⃣ 🔬 Fuel-cell optionality
Management says technology-licensing access remains intact and expects a commercialisation update next quarter, potentially covering a first-client timeline.

📌 Await formal disclosures before assigning revenue expectations.

⚠️ Key monitorables: Q4 commissioning, utilisation ramp-up, L1 conversion, funding execution and cash generation. Capacity-based revenue potential should be assessed separately from annual guidance.

Wer die Augen und Ohren vor der Realität verschließt, die Bilder und Rufe auf den Straßen Irans ignoriert und den Namen und das Bild jenes Mannes ausblendet, den ein großer Teil der iranischen Bevölkerung als seine politische Hoffnung und Wahl betrachtet, hat keinerlei Recht, im Namen des iranischen Volkes zu sprechen.

Von welchem iranischen Volk sprechen Sie eigentlich? Von den Menschen, die auf den Straßen Irans den Namen Reza Pahlavis rufen, seine Bilder und die Bilder der Pahlavi-Familie hochhalten und die Löwen-und-Sonne-Flagge zum Symbol ihres Widerstands gemacht haben? Oder von jenen kleinen politischen Kreisen im Ausland, die glauben, durch offene Briefe und Protesterklärungen den Willen einer Gesellschaft bestimmen zu können, die seit Jahrzehnten den Preis für den Kampf gegen die Islamische Republik bezahlt?

Das iranische Volk braucht weder Ihre Zustimmung noch die Anerkennung Ihrer politischen Zirkel, um seinen Willen zum Ausdruck zu bringen. Die Straßen Irans, die Rufe der Menschen und der hohe Preis, den sie für ihre Freiheit zahlen, sprechen eine deutlichere Sprache als die Erklärungen politischer Kreise im Ausland.

Wo waren Sie mit Ihrer Empörung, als Zehntausende Iranerinnen und Iraner von diesem Regime ermordet wurden? Wo war Ihre Stimme angesichts der Opfer, der trauernden Familien, der politischen Gefangenen und der Menschen, die täglich unter der Repression der Islamischen Republik leiden? Warum ist Ihre Empörung ausgerechnet dann so laut, wenn es darum geht, die Wahl eines politischen Repräsentanten infrage zu stellen?

Menschenrechte, Freiheit und Demokratie dürfen keine selektiven Prinzipien sein. Man kann nicht ständig von Demokratie sprechen und gleichzeitig die Stimmen jener Menschen ignorieren, die sich offen gegen die Islamische Republik stellen und ihren politischen Willen deutlich zum Ausdruck bringen.

Das Schweigen angesichts der Verbrechen und die gleichzeitige Hervorhebung der Stimmen sogenannter Schein-Oppositioneller, die keinerlei Legitimität in der iranischen Bevölkerung genießen, kommen in der Praxis genau jenem Regime zugute, das den Iranerinnen und Iranern ihre Freiheit genommen hat.
Eine solche Haltung ist keine Verteidigung der Demokratie. Sie ist politische Verantwortungslosigkeit.

Anders als diese Kreise hat die Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung für die Freiheit Weitblick bewiesen. Dafür gebührt ihr und insbesondere ihrem Vorstandsvorsitzenden Steffen Saebisch unser ausdrücklicher Dank und unsere Anerkennung.

Die Entscheidung, den Freiheitspreis 2026 dem iranischen Volk zu widmen und Prinz @PahlaviReza mit der stellvertretenden Entgegennahme zu betrauen, ist ein bedeutendes und begrüßenswertes Signal. Die Stiftung hat damit nicht nur den Freiheitskampf der Iranerinnen und Iraner gewürdigt, sondern auch verstanden, dass ihre Stimme nicht durch politische Lobbygruppen im Ausland ersetzt werden darf.

Besonders wichtig ist die Klarstellung der Stiftung, dass der Preis dem iranischen Volk gehört und zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt den frei gewählten Vertreterinnen und Vertretern eines freien Irans übergeben werden soll.

Unser Dank gilt @StSaebisch und allen Verantwortlichen der Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung, die den Mut und die Weitsicht hatten, die Stimme des iranischen Volkes zu hören und eine Entscheidung zu treffen, die den Hoffnungen vieler Iranerinnen und Iraner gerecht wird.

Die Geschichte wird darüber urteilen, wer an der Seite des iranischen Volkes stand und wer sich geweigert hat, seine Stimme zu hören.

Für ein freies, geeintes und selbstbestimmtes Iran.

What can change is your class position (your relation to property and labour) and your class standpoint (whose interests you organize your life around) but the test is not mere declaration. You have to make a genuine "break" with the class of your origin.

Intellectual break. Seeing that your own class’s interests rest on exploitation, and that your emancipation is tied to abolishing class society rather than climbing within it.

Material break. Conviction alone proves little. Amilcar Cabral called this “class suicide”: giving up privilege, property, security and career, and accepting the risks that the working class faces. Without it, the position remains bourgeois even when the language is revolutionary.

Organizational subordination. The most reliable test is whether the person accepts discipline and accountability to a working-class base and its organization, rather than leading as a benevolent patron. Gramsci’s idea of the “organic intellectual” fits here: someone who emerges from and is answerable to a class, rather than floating above it.

Immersion and re-education. Mao insisted that intellectuals had to learn from workers and peasants through shared work and life. Habits of speech, assumptions, ease with authority, and a sense of entitlement outlast ideological conversion, which is why Bourdieu’s point about habitus matters.

Time and proof. Credibility is earned through years of conduct, especially under pressure, not by declaration.

Those who defect from the bourgeoisie can slide into substitutionism, speaking for the working class instead of building its capacity to speak for itself, and into paternalism. Many socialist movements have also been damaged by leaders whose privilege reasserted itself once they held power. That’s why movements place so much weight on collective control and accountability instead of trusting personal virtue.

In India there is a further layer. Dr. Ambedkar’s critique of the Left was that upper-caste leaders could shed class privilege in theory while carrying caste privilege untouched, in networks, assumptions, and who gets heard and trusted. So the break has to be a caste break as well as a class break, and where it isn’t, the working-class base is correct to be suspicious. This is part of why the Bahujan tradition emphasizes leadership emerging from the oppressed themselves rather than being delivered from above.

The upshot is that origin is not destiny, but class change is a process of material sacrifice and accountable practice rather than a single act of conversion.

Note: I get annoyed when I have to explain such basic things to self-proclaimed leftists with ZERO PRAXIS because my time in valuable and the Bahujan Working Class has a much greater right over it than you all internet commies.

Er tat in den Jahren der #Corona krise genau das, wozu ihn der hippokratische Eid und sein Gewissen verpflichteten. Er achtete die freie Entscheidung sowie das Recht auf körperliche Selbstbestimmung seiner Patienten. Für die Justiz reichte dieser Dienst am Menschen jedoch aus, um die volle Härte des Staatsapparats gegen ihn in Gang zu setzen.
 
Was Heinrich Habig und seiner Familie angetan wurde, erinnert an Methoden finsterer Zeiten. Seine Praxis wurde von einem Großaufgebot bewaffneter Polizisten gestürmt, Patienten verhört und private Räume verwüstet. Monatelang überwachten Behörden den Praxiseingang mit Parabolmikrofonen und hörten Handys ab. Es folgten Kontosperrungen, der Entzug der Approbation, ein lebenslanges Berufsverbot sowie horrende Anwaltskosten, die seine wirtschaftliche Existenz vernichteten.
 
Insgesamt saß Dr. Habig 26 Monate im Gefängnis, davon 16 Monate in quälender Untersuchungshaft. Erst vor wenigen Monaten kam er unter Bewährungsauflagen frei. Sein angebliches Vergehen: Er weigerte sich, gesunde Menschen gegen ihren Willen in ein medizinisches Experiment zu drängen, und schützte sie vor staatlichem Zwang.
Dieser Fall beweist unmissverständlich, dass von einer echten Aufarbeitung der Unrechtsmaßnahmen keine Rede sein kann. 📑 Advait Energy Transitions Limited — Investor Presentation Analysis (H1FY27)

🏢 Business Overview:
Advait Energy Transitions Limited (formerly Advait Infratech Limited; BSE: 543230, NSE: ADVAIT) is an Ahmedabad-based integrated energy infrastructure company founded in 2009 by Managing Director Shalin Sheth, listed on BSE SME in 2020 and migrated to BSE Mainboard in July 2023 and NSE Mainboard in January 2026.

It operates across two segments: (1) Power Transmission Solutions (PTS) — its established revenue-generating core — covering manufacturing of OPGW (Optical Ground Wire), ACS wires, Emergency Restoration Systems (ERS), and stringing tools, plus EPC services for High Ampacity Conductor (HAC) reconductoring, live-line OPGW installation, and RDSS (Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) distribution projects; the company has served 45+ countries, completed 460+ projects, and installed 25,000+ km of live-line OPGW.

(2) New and Renewable Energy (NRE) — an emerging vertical under subsidiary AGPL — covering manufacturing and EPC for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), alkaline electrolysers, PEM fuel cells, and Green Hydrogen (GH2) solutions, alongside an asset-ownership platform for IPP BESS and hybrid projects, and a carbon/I-REC services business.

Competitive moat: In PTS, Advait has built meaningful niche advantages. It claims ~50% market share in stringing tools supply and ~30% in insulators historically, supported by early manufacturing investment including a JV with TG China for OPGW/OFS production.

Advait produced India's first indigenously developed ERS for 33 kV–800 kV lines. Its execution record in high-complexity projects — 250 km OPGW stringing at 12,500 ft altitude in Leh and 4,500 km live-line OPGW stringing for UPPTCL — differentiates it from lower-complexity EPC peers.

GETCO (Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation) awarded Advait its first-ever HAC reconductoring EPC project, confirming expanding capability recognition.

In NRE, the moat is embryonic: Advait commissioned India's first 30 MW Make-in-India alkaline electrolyser semi-assembly facility at Kadi, Gujarat, and entered a strategic manufacturing partnership for electrolysers and fuel cells — first-mover positions, but commercial scale and customer depth remain unproven.

Margin trajectory and expansion: EBITDA margins peaked at 18.7% in FY24 (revenue ₹209 Cr), then compressed to 14.8% in FY25 and 13.6% in FY26 (revenue ₹715 Cr), likely reflecting NRE capability build-up costs and a higher EPC revenue mix at lower unit margins.

H1FY27 shows a recovery to 14.17% EBITDA margin, with EBITDA growing 82.6% YoY (₹31.06 Cr → ₹56.71 Cr) against revenue growth of 45.4% (₹275.30 Cr → ₹400.21 Cr) — a clear operating leverage effect.

Management described this as 'a significant improvement in profitability' driven by 'execution, operational efficiency and strengthening the fundamentals.' Full recovery to FY24-level margins (18–19%) likely depends on the Gangad gigafactory (Phase 1 targeting Q4 FY27) delivering manufacturing-scale cost savings and NRE backlog converting at higher-margin rates.

🔀 Strategic Shift:
Pivoting from niche T&D products/EPC to integrated energy transition platform; NRE now ~32% of ₹1,574.8 Cr order book; expanding into BESS manufacturing, electrolysers, GH2 EPC, and IPP asset ownership

✨ Key Highlights:
🔹 H1FY27 operating EBITDA grew 82.6% YoY against revenue growth of 45.4%, demonstrating clear operating leverage; management described H1FY27 as 'encouraging' with a 'significant improvement in profitability'
🔹 Order book grew from ₹1,303.6 Cr at FY26 end to ₹1,574.8 Cr by September 30, 2026, with NRE now representing ~32% (₹509.93 Cr) of the total — a signal that the newer energy transition business is gaining traction alongside the established PTS business
🔹 Commissioned India's first 30 MW Make-in-India Electrolyser Semi-Assembly Facility at Kadi, Gujarat — marks AETL's entry into domestic electrolyser manufacturing ahead of anticipated Green Hydrogen policy momentum
🔹 Initiated first IPP BESS project with a prominent Indian electricity organization — marks a strategic pivot from pure B2B services toward asset ownership in energy storage

Prizor's success will depend on converting its manufacturing investments and distribution network into sustainable revenue and cash flow. The company needs to increase capacity utilisation, expand its dealer network and strengthen its presence in institutional markets. It should also focus on developing higher value products rather than competing only on price.Successful development of its indigenous semiconductor chip could strengthen its competitive position, but the company must first demonstrate that the technology is commercially viable. Most importantly, revenue growth should translate into higher profits and stronger operating cash flow.
A business that grows rapidly while continuously increasing debt may struggle to create long term shareholder value.

The commissioning of Prizor's additional manufacturing capacity in July 2026 marks an important transition from expansion plans to actual execution. The company has increased annual assembly capacity from 16 lakh units to 24 lakh units.
This is significant because Prizor has already demonstrated strong demand and revenue growth. The next stage is to convert its expanded manufacturing capacity into higher sales, profits and cash flow. The indigenous semiconductor chip could eventually become an even bigger technological turning point. However, the most important development to monitor today is whether Prizor can successfully utilise its expanded manufacturing capacity while maintaining margins and controlling working capital.

Prizor Viztech is therefore attempting to transform itself from an import driven surveillance brand into a more integrated Indian manufacturer. Its rapid revenue growth, expanding dealer network, healthy margins and manufacturing investments are encouraging. The biggest opportunities lie in increasing manufacturing utilisation, benefiting from domestic surveillance demand, expanding into higher value AI products and reducing dependence on imported components. However, the company is still much smaller than established competitors and faces meaningful working capital, debt and execution risks. The key question for investors is no longer whether Prizor can grow its revenue. It is whether the company can convert that growth into sustainable profits and strong cash generation.

Demanding Valuation:

At nearly 69 times earnings, the market is already pricing in substantial future growth.
Prizor's business prospects are encouraging, but the stock is no longer available at a modest valuation. The market is already assigning a premium to its growth potential. The key question is whether the company can grow its profits fast enough to justify this premium.
Strong execution could support the valuation, but any disappointment in revenue growth, margins or working capital could lead to a sharp correction.

From an Import Driven Brand to an Indian Surveillance Manufacturer

Business Model:

Prizor Viztech designs, manufactures and sells CCTV cameras, video recorders and other surveillance equipment under its own brand.

Its products reach customers through a network of more than 11,000 dealers across 21 to 22 states. These dealers supply local installers, shops and institutional customers.This distribution model allows Prizor to expand its reach without having to establish its own retail outlets across the country.

The company also sells televisions, monitors and touch panels but these are manufactured by third party partners. Surveillance products remain its main business.

The biggest change is that Prizor is gradually moving from importing components and assembling cameras towards manufacturing more of its products in India. Its Gandhinagar facility includes circuit board assembly, plastic housing moulding, camera manufacturing and laser branding. This allows the company to control more of the manufacturing process and potentially retain a larger share of the value created.

Prizor has grown rapidly over the last three years. Revenue increased from approximately ₹13.8 crore in FY23 to ₹147.94 crore in FY26. Net profit increased from just ₹30 lakh to ₹20.76 crore during the same period. Its dealer network has more than doubled in two years, increasing from approximately 5,200 dealers to over 11,000. CCTV camera sales grew 152% during FY26, reflecting the increasing contribution of its core business.

The company reported an EBITDA margin of 22.5% in FY26, while its H1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 23.6%. Its H1 FY27 revenue increased 153% to ₹106.5 crore, while net profit grew 159% to ₹15.3 crore.
The company has also commissioned an additional assembly line, increasing annual assembly capacity from 16 lakh units to 24 lakh units.

Prizor's biggest competitive advantage is the combination of its own manufacturing facility, expanding dealer network and certifications required for selling surveillance products in India.
The government has introduced stricter certification requirements for surveillance equipment. This creates an opportunity for domestic manufacturers that can meet the required standards.

Prizor has obtained BIS and STQC related certifications for multiple camera models.
However, certification alone does not guarantee market leadership. Larger competitors such as CP Plus and Hikvision India also have certified products.

Prizor is not a monopoly and is not the market leader. Its CCTV revenue of approximately ₹114 crore in FY26 represents only a small share of the Indian surveillance market.

Its reported margins suggest that it can earn reasonable profits, but this does not necessarily mean it has strong pricing power.

The surveillance industry remains competitive, and customers can choose from several brands.

Aditya Infotech, which owns the CP Plus brand, is also listed in India. Prizor is listed on the NSE SME platform and is much smaller than established competitors.
Its opportunity is to build a stronger position by offering reliable products, expanding distribution and increasing local manufacturing.

Profit growth is not yet translating into strong cash generation. Prizor reported FY26 net profit of ₹20.76 crore, but operating cash flow was only approximately ₹29 lakh.This suggests that a significant amount of money is getting tied up in inventory and customer receivables.
The company needs to demonstrate that its growth can generate cash, not just accounting profits.

Working capital requirements are increasing.Short term borrowings reportedly increased from ₹2.8 crore to ₹31.8 crore. This is important because rapid growth can become difficult to sustain if the company has to borrow heavily to finance inventory and dealer credit.

posts.text: @wegro_app Advait Energy Transitions has released its Q2 and H1 FY27 investor presentation, showcasing key highlights for the period ended September 30, 2026. You and  @mukilan46998215  are the two accounts I most enjoy following.

𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗶𝘁 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗟𝘁𝗱: 𝗤2 & 𝗛1 𝗙𝗬27 𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 📊 :
Advait Energy Transitions Ltd has released its investor presentation for the quarter & half-year ended September 30, 2026, showcasing robust financial performance & strategic advancements.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵:
  ▸ Q2 FY27: ₹220.9 Cr, up 40.8% YoY & 23.2% QoQ.
  ▸ H1 FY27: ₹400.2 Cr, up 45.4% YoY.
- 𝗘𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗗𝗔 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝗴𝗲:
  ▸ Q2 FY27: ₹31.9 Cr, up 84.4% YoY & 28.9% QoQ.
  ▸ H1 FY27: ₹56.7 Cr, up 82.6% YoY.
- 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁 𝗔𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗮𝘅 (𝗣𝗔𝗧):
  ▸ Q2 FY27: ₹19.2 Cr, up 88.5% YoY & 29.6% QoQ.
  ▸ H1 FY27: ₹34.0 Cr, up 77.9% YoY.
- 𝗢𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻:
  ▸ As of Sep 30, 2026, the order book stands at ₹1,574.8 Cr, marking a significant 47% YoY increase. Power Transmission Solutions (PTS) constitute 68% & New & Renewable Energy (NRE) 32%.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀 & 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝘀:

- 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 (𝗣𝗧𝗦): Secured orders worth ~₹462 Cr in Q2 FY27, including underground cabling & Emergency Restoration Systems (ERS).
- 𝗡𝗲𝘄 & 𝗥𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 (𝗡𝗥𝗘): Won a ₹116 Cr solar EPC order for a 200 MW project. The company is also setting up a 2.5 GWh BESS assembly facility backed by an MSA with Hithium for battery cells.
- 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀: Advait is actively participating in India's energy transition, expanding into Green Hydrogen, BESS, and Solar EPC. The company highlights its strategic evolution into an integrated growth ecosystem with an asset ownership platform.
- 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗳𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀: Expanding capacities for High Ampacity Conductors (HAC), BESS, Electrolysers, & Fuel Cells. A new 4,00,000+ sq. ft. facility is under development.

𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 & 𝗕𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗦𝗵𝗲𝗲𝘁 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗴𝘁𝗵:

- 𝗘𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗗𝗔 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁: Consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 14.45% in Q2 FY27 (+342 bps YoY).
- 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀: Capital work-in-progress stood at ₹159.71 Cr, indicating ongoing capacity expansion.
- 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗥𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝘀: Debt-equity was 0.86x & interest coverage 5.73x, with a continued focus on working capital management.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀:

- Signed an MSA with Hithium for up to 1 GWh of LFP battery cells.
- Entered an MoU with RNH Ventures, Sri Lanka, to explore clean energy opportunities & establish a distribution arrangement.

The presentation underscores Advait's commitment to execution, operational efficiency, & building long-term shareholder value amidst India's evolving energy landscape. 🚀

Stop getting satisfied with 20%, 30%, 40% or even 50% returns. Start thinking BIG. I'm talking about identifying potential 5X–10X opportunities, especially 8X–10X multibaggers.

And remember, exceptional returns don't come from reacting to premium news or quarterly results.

They come from identifying a good company in a promising sector, buying it at an attractive valuation with good management, or playing a genuine turnaround story.

These returns will not come from reacting to quarterly results. They come from understanding businesses and anticipating opportunities.

India’s Future Tech Builders – Week 3

India wants 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen a year by 2030. But almost nobody is talking about the machine that makes it. One small-cap from Gujarat is building that machine — and it just matched L&T and Reliance on a key government metric.

Let me tell you about Advait Energy Transitions (NSE: ADVAIT), formerly Advait Infratech.

This is not a defence company. This is not a semiconductor play. This is a power transmission business that quietly walked into green hydrogen, and is now building electrolysers on Indian soil.

Here is the breakdown.

What they are doing right
They are not a startup chasing a subsidy. They have been in power transmission since 2009. Their core business is OPGW cables, stringing tools, emergency restoration systems, and live-line installations.

That last part is the moat. Advait is one of the very few companies in India that can do live-line OPGW installation on energised 220 kV lines. They have executed high-altitude projects in Ladakh. That is not a commodity business. That is rare execution capability.

And that core business is funding the green hydrogen bet.

On electrolysers, the progress is real:
- Phase I of their 30 MW alkaline electrolyser assembly facility in Gujarat was commissioned in March 2026. It is the foundation for a 100 MW Phase II and a fully automated 300 MW Phase III complex.
- They hold 300 MW of annual electrolyser manufacturing capacity under the government's SIGHT programme — 100 MW in Tranche-I and 200 MW in Tranche-II.
- They completed a 1 MW green hydrogen facility in Gujarat and became the first domestic firm to demonstrate live testing of a 5 MW electrolyser with verified Specific Energy Consumption metrics.

The order book tells the story. FY26 revenue came in at ₹714.52 crore, up 79.68%. PAT grew 75% to ₹58.08 crore. The order book crossed ₹1,304 crore, up 159% year-on-year. And there is an active tender pipeline of around ₹2,000 crore.
They are also building BESS capacity. A 50 MW/100 MWh project for GUVNL, a 150 MW/300 MWh project in Junagadh, and a planned integrated manufacturing hub at Gangad with 2.5 GWh of BESS assembly and 300 MW of electrolyser production.

What is going in their favour
The policy wind is the strongest it has ever been. India's National Green Hydrogen Mission has a ₹19,744 crore outlay and a target of 5 million metric tonnes per annum by 2030. Under SIGHT, 15 companies have been awarded a combined 3,000 MW of annual electrolyser manufacturing capacity. Advait is one of them.

The grid upgrade cycle is also structural. India is committing nearly ₹9 lakh crore to modernise and expand power transmission infrastructure. Advait's core business sits directly in that spend.

And the domestic manufacturing push is real. Every green hydrogen project in India needs electrolysers. Importing them is expensive and slow. Advait is building the capacity to make them here.

How they can prove they are the company of the future
Matching L&T and Reliance on a 300 MW SIGHT metric is a headline. But a headline is not a business.

They need to convert their enquiry pipeline into firm orders. Management estimates a 150–200 MW electrolyser supply opportunity based on active enquiries from green ammonia players. That is enquiry-driven, not confirmed. The next twelve months must turn that into signed contracts.
They need to make the Gangad integrated manufacturing hub operational. The 300 MW electrolyser complex is expected to come online in Q4 FY27, along with BESS and PEM fuel-cell manufacturing. Execution on that timeline is everything.

They need to move from semi-assembly to integrated manufacturing. They have exclusive Indian rights to Jiangsu Guofu's electrolyser designs, which helped them move quickly. The next step is deeper indigenous content and cost control.

Where they need to be careful
Here is where I get uncomfortable.

The working capital cycle is stretched. Debtor days stand at 173. That is a lot of cash locked up in receivables. For a company growing at this pace, cash flow discipline matters more than revenue growth.

Margins have compressed. Operating margins moved from around 17% to roughly 11% as the business mix shifted. Some of that is the cost of scaling. But it needs to stabilise.
This is still a small-cap. Market cap is around ₹1,687 crore. The stock trades at a P/E of about 42, which is not outrageous for the sector, but the price can swing sharply. Promoter holding also declined slightly last quarter. Worth watching.

And the green hydrogen demand cycle in India is still developing. Capacity is ramping, but offtake is not yet at scale. A small-cap building a 300 MW facility ahead of demand carries execution risk.

Who they are actually competing with
This is not a crowded niche. The names here are giants.

1. L&T Electrolysers has 300 MW of SIGHT capacity and is integrating electrolyser manufacturing into its existing engineering and EPC muscle. They can bundle electrolysers with green ammonia and green methanol projects. That is a different level of balance sheet.
2. Reliance Electrolyser Manufacturing also has 300 MW and sits inside a much larger new-energy ecosystem — solar, batteries, green fuels. They are building the entire value chain, not just one piece of equipment.
3. Waaree Energies won a ₹444 crore PLI for a 300 MW electrolyser facility and is committing about ₹676 crore to a 1 GW alkaline plant in Gujarat. That is serious capital.
Ohmium is a global PEM electrolyser player with 137 MW of SIGHT allocation. Matrix Gas and Renewables has 237 MW. NewAge Green Electro has 300 MW across two tranches. Adani Enterprises and BHEL are also on the SECI list.

Sterling and Wilson and INOX India are adjacent plays in the broader green hydrogen ecosystem.

How they can leave the competition behind
Advait cannot outspend L&T or Reliance. So it has to out-execute them on speed and focus.

Be the fastest to deliver. L&T and Reliance are building large, integrated programmes. Advait's advantage is agility. If they can commission the Gangad hub on time and deliver electrolysers faster than the giants, they become the default supplier for projects that cannot wait.
Own the EPC layer. Advait already does EPC for green hydrogen projects. That means they can sell the electrolyser and build the plant. L&T can do this too, but Reliance is focused on its own projects. Being the independent EPC-plus-equipment partner for third-party green hydrogen developers is a real positioning.

Win the 150–200 MW enquiry pipeline. This is the near-term battle. Converting those enquiries into orders before Waaree or Ohmium locks in the customers is what separates a story from a business.

Keep the core business strong. The power transmission business funds the hydrogen bet. Do not let the green hydrogen ambition distract from the OPGW and live-line execution that pays the bills.

My advice: Prove the 30 MW first, then scale
I would not say stop. I would say sequence.

Make the 30 MW facility run at full utilisation. Convert the 5 MW test batch into commercial orders. Prove that the electrolysers work, that customers are paying, and that the unit economics hold.
Then scale to 100 MW and 300 MW. Then build the BESS and fuel-cell layers on top.

The ambition is right. The order is what matters.

Final thought
Advait Energy Transitions is at an inflection point. They proved a small-cap from Gujarat can win a 300 MW SIGHT allocation alongside L&T and Reliance. They proved they can commission an electrolyser facility and test a 5 MW stack. Now they need to prove they can sell it at scale and get paid on time.

If the electrolyser orders convert and the Gangad hub comes online as planned, this becomes a serious energy-transition story. If working capital and margins stay stretched, the story gets harder.

I am watching the 150–200 MW enquiry conversion and the debtor days very closely. You should too.

Revenue growth aspiration 20-25% (H1: 27%)

8.  Key Risks

Weak consumer demand
Price rises
Floods in Bihar
High Bihar exposure

Urban Company का देश की महिलाओं के साथ अत्याचार :

महिला को Customer के घर भेजने और उससे कमाई कंपनी की, लेकिन महिला सुरक्षा की जिम्मेदारी किसी की नहीं?

@urbancompany_UC के अपने T&C का Clause 2(c) कहता है कि Company Professional की Safety, Security और Welfare के लिए जिम्मेदार नहीं है!

जरा इस व्यवस्था को समझिए—

▪️ Company job Booking खुद लेती है और महिला कामगार को अनजान Customer के घर भेजती है।
और महिला कामगार को जॉब को मना करने पर कैंसलेशन मार्क करने का दवाब बनाती है 

▪️ जब कोई महिला Partner इमरजेंसी में Customer Executive को कॉल करती है, तो कई बार कॉल ही नहीं लगता। काफी देर कोशिश करने के बाद संपर्क हो भी जाए, तो मदद मिलने के बजाय Customer Executive द्वारा महिला Partner पर ही दोष डालने की कोशिश किए जाने की शिकायतें सामने आती हैं।
यह केवल खराब Customer Support का मामला नहीं है। किसी महिला की सुरक्षा खतरे में हो और उस समय कंपनी का सहायता तंत्र ही काम न करे, तो स्थिति बेहद गंभीर हो सकती है।

▪️ Customer का फोन बंद हो, गलत पता हो या जगह असुरक्षित हो, तब भी Job को deliver करने का दवाब बनाया जाता है और महिला पार्टनर को कस्टमर की लोकेशन पर जाने के लिए मजबूर किया जाता है । और कैंसलेशन लगाने का डर दुखिया जाता है आईडी ब्लॉक करने का डर दिखाया जाता है ।

महिला को Threat, Harassment या Assault का सामना करना पड़े तो तत्काल मदद और जवाबदेही की कोई भी व्यवस्था नहीं है बस इमरजेंसी कॉल का ऑप्शन दिया है वहाँ पर कोई भी मदद नहीं मिलती है कॉल ही नहीं मिलता है और जब मिलता है यो कोई मदद नहीं नहीं मिलती ना ही कोई इसके बारे में प्रोटोकॉल फिक्स किया हुआ है की इस सिचुएशन में कैसे और किस स्तर तक मदद की जाएगी । अपने क्लॉज़ का हवाला देकर कंपनी अपना पल्ला झाड़ लेती है ।

सवाल यह है कि अगर कंपनी ग्राहक की बुकिंग लेती है, महिला कामगार को उसके घर भेजती है और काम से जुड़े नियम व प्रदर्शन नियंत्रित करती है, तो उसकी सुरक्षा के लिए केवल एक Emergency Call बटन देकर जिम्मेदारी पूरी कैसे मानी जा सकती है?

यानी Customer तक पहुँचाने और Job पूरी करवाने के लिए Platform सक्रिय है, लेकिन महिला की सुरक्षा का सवाल आते ही Company अपने Terms & Conditions के पीछे खड़ी हो जाती है!

यह कैसी Partnership है, जिसमें महिला अपनी मेहनत के साथ अपनी सुरक्षा का जोखिम भी खुद उठाए?
हम @LabourMinistry @CLCMOLE @NCWIndia @MinistryWCD @NITIAayog से मांग करते हैं कि Urban Company की Safety Policies, Customer Verification, Emergency Assistance और महिला कामगारों पर लागू दंडात्मक व्यवस्थाओं की स्वतंत्र एवं निष्पक्ष जाँच कराई जाए।

@urbancompany_UC और उसके शीर्ष प्रबंधन को सोचना चाहिए आपकी कंपनी के पीछे काम करने वाली महिला की सुरक्षा की कोई गारंटी और जवाबदेही है या नहीं?
महिला सशक्तिकरण केवल विज्ञापनों से नहीं, कामगारों को सुरक्षित और सम्मानजनक कार्यस्थल देने से होता है।

देश की महिलाओं से पूछते हैं क्या ऐसी व्यवस्था को महिला सशक्तिकरण कहा जा सकता है, जहाँ महिला की मेहनत की कीमत तो तय है, लेकिन उसकी सुरक्षा की जवाबदेही स्पष्ट नहीं?
